head: d518ab6
target: A run refuses a secret or model key shorter than 8 characters, before the first session opens.
incidental: the design page restating the new rule in its invariant and verification lines
the test that adds a short secret and a short key to the refused scenario
the CLI test's longer dummy key

questions.prompt: A scenario's secret is set to three characters. What does the run do now?

options.label: It runs the scenario, and the redaction keeps the saved run readable.
It reports the secret as a problem before the first session opens.
It sends the value to the model and records the failure in the log.
It writes the run, then fails when the saved files are read back.

key_points: A short secret or model key is reported as a scenario problem before the first session opens.
No model call is spent and nothing is written.
The model key is checked the same way as the scenario's secrets.

questions.prompt: A one-character secret used to break the run at the very end, after the model had been called. Why?
key_points: The redaction replaces each raw secret value wherever it occurs in the log, keys included.
A one-character value sits inside ordinary words, so the redaction rewrote words and keys.
The saved run then fails to read back, so the failure lands after the model calls are spent.

questions.prompt: A new scenario sets a secret whose value is the common word 'scenario', eight characters long. Which of these hold?

options.label: The check rejects the value, because it matches ordinary words.
The length check passes, and the run starts.
The saved run is safe, because the value passed the check.
The redaction still rewrites the word wherever it occurs, keys included.

key_points: The check keys on length only, so an eight-character value passes it.
The redaction still rewrites the value wherever it occurs, including the log's keys.
The floor blocks degenerate short values, not every collision between a value and the run's text.
